dark.name: VerilogVsSystemVerilog
dark.text: Compare Verilog vs. SystemVerilog Select a feature to compare the Verilog-2001 way with the SystemVerilog way. ◇ Conceptual illustration Assumptions and limits Data Types Object Oriented Programming Assertions Randomization Verilog (IEEE 1364-2001) reg [7:0] a; // variable wire [7:0] b; // net integer i; reg (and integer, time, real) for variables, wire for nets. You choose reg or wire by how the signal is assigned, not by whether it is a register. No structs, enums or typedef. SystemVerilog (IEEE 1800) logic [7:0] a; // 4-state, same type as reg bit [7:0] b; // 2-state typedef enum {IDLE, RUN} state_t; struct { int x, y; } point; logic replaces reg as the descriptive name (§6.11.2). Adds 2-state bit, byte and int, and user-defined types: typedef, enum, struct, union. Backward compatible? Try a legacy file. // legacy.v: legal Verilog-2001 module legacy; reg [7:0] logic; // 'logic' was an ordinary name endmodule With no directive at all, the keyword set is the tool's default, which the standard leaves implementation dependent (§22.14). PredictYou compile legacy.v with an IEEE 1800 (SystemVerilog) keyword set and no directives in the file. What happens? It compiles. SystemVerilog accepts all Verilog code. Compile error: logic is a reserved keyword in SystemVerilog. It compiles, and the signal silently becomes a 4-state logic type. A warning only: the tool renames the signal for you. Lock in prediction Reveal without predicting SystemVerilog contains all of Verilog: IEEE 1800-2009 was a merger of IEEE 1364-2005 and IEEE 1800-2005 (IEEE 1800-2023 1.3 NOTE). But it is not a drop-in superset for every legacy file. New reserved keywords such as logic, bit, int and class break old code that used them as names, unless you use `begin_keywords.

dark.name: InterviewQuestionPlayground
dark.text: Interview angle: is UVM part of SystemVerilog? Is UVM part of the SystemVerilog standard? Yes. The UVM classes are defined in IEEE 1800-2023 Clause 8, with the other built-in classes. No. UVM is IEEE 1800.2-2020, a class library written in SystemVerilog and imported from uvm_pkg. No. UVM is a separate verification language, with its own compiler and runtime. Partly. UVM is a simulator feature that each vendor adds to its SystemVerilog tool. Submit answer

dark.name: InterviewQuestionPlayground
dark.text: Interview angle: a port named logic Your SystemVerilog testbench must connect to a legacy Verilog module whose output port is named logic. What do you do? Write .logic(q): the port is declared in the legacy file, so the name is legal everywhere. Compile the whole project, testbench included, with the Verilog-2001 keyword set. Nothing: the tool renames identifiers that clash with keywords automatically. Wrap the legacy file in a begin_keywords pair, and connect with .\logic (q) or by position. Submit answer

dark.name: InterviewQuestionPlayground
dark.text: Interview angle: adopting 2023 features Your team wants to use IEEE 1800-2023 features, such as triple-quoted strings and weak references, in a shared testbench. What do you check first? Nothing: every simulator supports each new IEEE revision from the day it is published. Whether begin_keywords "1800-2023" turns the new features on for the shared files. Whether every tool in the flow supports each feature, at the versions the team actually uses. Only that the simulator comes from a large vendor, since large vendors track the standard. Submit answer
